title: Org Structure (Departments & People)
markdown:
The org model has two persistent registries backed by SQLite (both share `episodic_memory.db`): **departments** and **people**. Eight default departments are seeded exactly once per database on first boot, tracked by a `default_departments_seeded` sentinel in `departments_meta`; after that the user owns the list and deleted departments stay deleted across restarts.

### Company setup (onboarding)
Both registries are first populated by **conversational onboarding** at
`/onboard`. The user describes their business in their own words (optionally
attaching a deck or one-pager); the `onboarding_interviewer` agent — Council-
visible but outside `SPECIALIST_REGISTRY`, so the Executive cannot reach it via
`consult_specialist` — asks up to 8 clarifying questions, then emits a draft
company profile, a leadership roster, and a department list. The user reviews
and edits that draft inline (the same section editors `/company-profile` uses)
before anything is written.

Two properties matter here. First, **the interview never writes**: the whole
exchange lives in an in-memory, TTL'd session, and the single write happens at
`POST /onboard/interview/commit`, so a rejected save leaves the draft editable
and retryable. Second, **the department step is additive** — drafted
departments are matched onto existing ones by slug or title and updated in
place, unmatched ones are created, and nothing is ever deleted. That is
deliberately unlike the fixture loader's `_seed_departments`, which DELETEs
every row first: doing that here would drop the eight defaults along with their
`specialist_key` wiring, which `create_department` (always `specialist_key =
NULL`) cannot restore. `profile.org_structure` is derived from the reviewed
people and department tables at commit time, so it cannot drift from them.

Exactly one person is marked `is_principal` and receives `WILDCARD` authority;
no contact details are imported, even if the user volunteers them, because
channels and handles are a deliberate action on the People page. The original
12-step form wizard remains available at `/onboard?mode=form` and backs the
`openexecutive onboard` CLI.

### Departments
Each department carries a charter, `Goal` rows, `ChecklistItem`s, and named cadences. Cadence specs (`daily@HH:MM`, `weekly@DOW@HH:MM`, `quarterly@DD-HH:MM`, UTC) enqueue a `department_check_in` workflow when due, then chain the next occurrence; `PATCH /departments/{slug}` rejects a spec that does not parse with a 422. A department may map to one of the 8 specialist agents via `specialist_key`, or stay informational. An assigned head gets a generated department-head voice persona.

A department can also list **watched entities** (`watched_entities`, edited one per line on its page): vendors it is evaluating, competitors in its lane, tickers it tracks. The research watch policy treats them as strong grounding — a proposal about one can be added to the watch list on its own — and routes the resulting watch, its alerts and any suggestion cards to the department and its head rather than the principal (see External monitoring).

### Authority gate
Each department declares an `AuthorityLevel`, which `departments.authority.gate_action` checks whenever a department-scoped scheduled action comes due. `auto_execute` (autonomous) fires directly. `propose_only` turns the action into an approval card for an approver (`propose_via_alert`) and sends nothing, deferring the card to the approver's next availability window when they are outside it. `escalate` also sends nothing until someone approves: it raises an urgent `[ESCALATION]` card right away, never deferred — what the Departments page promises ("the specialist will not act — it forwards everything to a human"). It used to raise the card *and* dispatch, so approving the card sent the action a second time. Calendar bookings follow the same rule. The approver is chosen by `AuthorityScope` — a scheduled action's `required_scope` (e.g. `vendor_onboarding`, `spend_lt_10k`) feeds `find_approvers(scope)`, which ranks non-principal scope-holders ahead of `WILDCARD` holders. A null/unknown scope falls back to `WILDCARD` (the principal).

### People & channels
The people registry resolves each `Person` to a `(channel, channel_ref)` pair via `prefer_channel_for()`, honoring `preferred_channel` (falling back email → slack → discord → telegram) and availability windows. Departments can also set `slack_channel_id` / `discord_channel_id` / `telegram_chat_id` to broadcast to a team room instead of DMing the head.

Each person's page also lists their **open loops** (see Attunement) — what they committed to or were asked for in conversation — with a *Mark done* action; archiving a person closes their open loops, since an archived person can no longer be chased. The list is the principal's or that person's only; `people.store.is_principal_or_self` is the one check behind it, the close action and reply feedback.

The Executive can change the roster from a chat turn (`upsert_person`, `archive_person`, `set_department_head`) only when the principal asks, from the web chat or their own Slack, Discord or Telegram. A teammate, an email (even one from the principal's address), Google Chat, the CLI, the MCP server and unattended runs are refused, because a People row is also the web sign-in allow-list, the outbound-email allow-list and approval routing. The People page itself is unaffected.

flowchart TD
  People["People registry (Person, is_principal)"]
  Dept["Departments (8 seeded once)"]
  GC["Goals / checklists / cadences"]
  Head["Head + voice persona"]
  Gate["Authority gate (propose_only vs autonomous)"]
  Scope["AuthorityScope to find_approvers"]
  Chan["Channel resolution (Discord / Telegram / email)"]
  Dept --> GC
  Dept --> Head
  Dept -->|proposes action| Gate
  Gate -->|required_scope| Scope
  Scope -->|ranks approvers| People
  People --> Chan
  Dept -->|team room| Chan

  class Dept storage
  class GC storage
  class Gate compute
  class Scope compute
  class Chan compute
